newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Unions, gov't close to deal on Colombian strike. [CORRECTED 15:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Unions, gov't close to deal on Colombian strike. [CORRECTED 15:27 GMT]

text.p: Union leaders and government officials were close to reaching a deal Monday to end the seven- day-old public sector strike after all-night negotiations.
Talks, which began just before midnight Sunday, are due to resume at 10 am (1500 GMT) Monday after a short recess but representatives said that both sides were now "very close".

"The talks were very interesting and the positions are now very close. It is always unwise to speak before the deal is actually signed but it is most likely that we will reach an agreement today," said Wilson Borja, head of the main state workers' union FENALTRASE.
He said the unions and government ministers were on the verge of a deal to review legal action being taken against a number of labor leaders and just a "short distance apart" on wage demands.

The government has already agreed that employees who took part in the strike would not be sanctioned when they returned to work. The main sticking point, Borja said, was the issue of the government's planned wave of privatizations of a number of regional and national industries.
State workers initially called the strike to press for a 21.5 percent (corrects from 13.5 percent) wage hike, compared to the government's sub- inflation offer of a weighted 13.5 percent.
Borja declined to say what the pay proposal was by the end of negotiations around dawn this morning.
"These were a few very positive and dynamic hours. We made a lot of ground and are now on the verge of an accord," Labor Minister Orlando Obregn told reporters.

The impact of the strike so far has been difficult to judge. President Ernesto Samper said just 10 percent of state workers had heeded the strike call while union heads said they had severely disrupted a number of key economic and social sectors.
